A HISTORY OF VIOLENCE (2005)
DETAILED SCREENPLAY-STYLE RETELLING
ORIGINAL RETELLING — NOT THE ORIGINAL SCREENPLAY

NOTE: This is an original, scene-oriented retelling of the film's story. It does not reproduce the copyrighted screenplay or dialogue.

========================================
ACT I — THE PEACEFUL LIFE
========================================

FADE IN:

EXT. RURAL AMERICAN TOWN — DAY

A quiet town.

People know one another.

TOM STALL lives here with his wife EDIE and their children.

Tom owns a small diner and has built a reputation as an ordinary, dependable man.

Nothing about him suggests a violent past.

INT. STALL FAMILY HOME — MORNING

Tom prepares for another ordinary day.

His relationship with his family is warm.

The family argues about everyday matters.

It is a life built around routine.

INT. DINER — DAY

Tom works behind the counter.

Customers know him.

The atmosphere is comfortable.

Then two violent criminals enter.

Their presence changes the room.

They threaten the people inside.

Tom attempts to keep everyone calm.

The situation escalates.

The criminals become increasingly dangerous.

Tom suddenly reacts.

His response is extraordinarily fast and precise.

He stops the attackers.

The people in the diner stare at him.

Tom himself seems disturbed by what he has just done.

EXT. DINER — LATER

Police arrive.

News of Tom's actions spreads quickly.

The local community celebrates him as a hero.

Reporters become interested.

Tom is uncomfortable with the attention.

He wants his normal life back.

INT. STALL FAMILY HOME — NIGHT

The family watches coverage of the incident.

Edie is proud but also curious.

Tom tries to dismiss the event.

But somewhere far away, someone sees the news.

A man recognizes Tom.

He believes Tom is someone from his own violent past.

CUT TO BLACK.

========================================
ACT II — THE PAST RETURNS
========================================

EXT. SMALL TOWN — DAY

A mysterious man arrives.

He watches Tom.

Tom notices him.

The stranger behaves as though he knows Tom intimately.

Tom denies knowing him.

But the encounter leaves Tom unsettled.

INT. STALL FAMILY HOME — NIGHT

Tom's family senses that something has changed.

Edie asks questions.

Tom offers explanations.

But the answers do not completely satisfy her.

EXT. TOWN — DAY

The stranger and his associates continue appearing.

Their presence makes Tom's ordinary world increasingly unsafe.

Tom tries to maintain his normal routine.

The effort becomes difficult.

INT. DINER — DAY

Tom works while customers talk about the recent events.

The community still sees him as a hero.

But Tom knows there is another story beneath the surface.

EXT. STREET — NIGHT

Another confrontation occurs.

Tom's old instincts return.

He survives.

But the way he fights makes it increasingly difficult to believe that he is simply the peaceful man everyone thinks he is.

INT. FAMILY HOME — NIGHT

Edie confronts Tom.

She wants the truth.

Tom's past is becoming impossible to hide.

The family begins to understand that the man they know may have once lived as someone else.

CUT TO:

EXT. CITY — DAY

Tom travels toward the people connected to his past.

He is no longer merely defending his current life.

He is confronting the identity he abandoned.

INT. BUILDING — DAY

Tom encounters someone who knows him from before.

The conversation forces buried memories into the open.

Tom's former identity was violent.

He had escaped that world and created a new life.

But the people from that life refuse to let him disappear.

========================================
ACT III — CONFRONTING THE PAST
========================================

EXT. RURAL PROPERTY — DAY

Tom arrives at a place connected to his former life.

The peaceful world he built is now far away.

He understands that running from the past will not make it disappear.

INT. HOUSE — DAY

Tom confronts the people who remain connected to his former identity.

The conflict becomes personal.

He is forced to use the abilities he hoped never to use again.

The confrontation reaches its final stage.

Tom survives.

But survival does not mean everything is repaired.

EXT. FAMILY HOME — NIGHT

Tom returns.

The danger has passed.

But his family has learned the truth.

There is a silence between them.

Tom has returned physically.

Emotionally, everything has changed.

INT. FAMILY HOME — DAY

The family sits together.

Nobody knows exactly what to say.

Tom is no longer simply the man they thought they knew.

Yet he is still their husband and father.

The family must decide how to live with the truth.

The story ends without pretending that violence leaves no consequences.

Tom's old life has been confronted.

But its shadow remains.

FADE OUT.

========================================
STRUCTURAL LESSON
========================================

Peaceful ordinary life
        ↓
Unexpected violent event
        ↓
Protagonist reveals hidden ability
        ↓
Someone recognizes him
        ↓
Mysterious people from the past arrive
        ↓
Family begins questioning him
        ↓
Hidden identity is revealed
        ↓
Protagonist confronts former world
        ↓
Final confrontation
        ↓
Survival
        ↓
Family faces the consequences
